retrieved_knowledge.title: Community-acquired pneumonia
retrieved_knowledge.content: Pneumonia is an infection of the lung tissue. Commonly described features include fever, cough (sometimes with sputum), breathlessness and chest pain that worsens with breathing. A raised white cell count and CRP are non-specific inflammatory markers that can accompany bacterial infection.
general_workup: Chest X-ray is commonly used to look for lung consolidation.
Pulse oximetry is used to assess oxygenation.
Sputum or blood cultures may be considered in some settings.

retrieved_knowledge.title: Interpreting inflammatory markers (WBC and CRP)
retrieved_knowledge.content: White cell count and CRP are non-specific markers. They can rise with bacterial infection, other inflammation or tissue injury, and may be normal early in illness. They support, but never establish, a diagnosis and are interpreted with clinical findings and trends over time.
general_workup: Repeat measurement can show the trend over time.

retrieved_knowledge.title: Urinary tract infection
retrieved_knowledge.content: Urinary tract infections commonly cause burning on urination, increased frequency and urgency, and lower abdominal discomfort. Fever and flank pain can suggest the infection has involved the kidneys.
general_workup: Urinalysis (dipstick and/or microscopy) is commonly used.
Urine culture helps identify the organism in many settings.

retrieved_knowledge.title: Influenza-like illness
retrieved_knowledge.content: Influenza commonly presents with abrupt fever, muscle aches, headache, fatigue and dry cough. Many other viral infections cause a similar picture, so the term influenza-like illness is used when the cause is not confirmed.
general_workup: Rapid influenza or respiratory viral testing may be considered depending on setting and season.
